transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Honestly, I feel like the warm part of me just shut off. I’ll sit with my husband or try to watch my shows after work, and I know I should feel comfort or maybe a little happy, but there’s just nothing there.
How long have you been feeling this way—like that 'warm part' has been shut off?
About three weeks now. It started after the pallet collapsed and my coworker got hurt.
Since the accident, have you had any unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about what happened to your coworker?
Yeah. It comes back out of nowhere—I’ll see the pallet falling again, or hear that crash in my head. Especially if a forklift beeps or someone drops something in the warehouse. My stomach just turns.
Have you found yourself avoiding certain places, sounds, or situations at work—like staying away from forklifts or certain areas—because they remind you of the accident?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself avoiding anything specific at work.
Since the accident, have you noticed feeling more on edge, jumpy, or easily startled, or having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, my sleep’s been bad. I’m exhausted after my late shift, but when I start to fall asleep, I’ll jerk awake thinking I heard pallets shifting. And when I do sleep, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.

Since the accident, have you ever felt like you were detached from your body or surroundings, like things felt unreal or like you were watching yourself from outside, or found you couldn't remember parts of what happened?

I don’t think things felt unreal, but there’s a part right after it fell that I just can’t remember. I remember the stack leaning and people yelling, then it’s blank. I know I must’ve moved or called for help, but I can’t piece that part together no matter how much I try.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself avoiding conversations, news, or thoughts about what happened, even outside of work?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself avoiding talking or thinking about it outside of work.
Has this emotional numbness and these sleep problems been affecting your ability to function at work or in your relationship with your husband?
Yeah. I’m not able to do my regular receiving work right now. During a pallet move I froze up, then I snapped at someone, and my supervisor took me off the floor because I wasn’t functioning safely.
